# Triton-XDNA Examples

These examples demonstrate how to write [Triton](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton) kernels that compile and run on AMD XDNA™ NPUs via the [MLIR-AIR](https://github.com/Xilinx/mlir-air) compilation flow.

## End-to-End Models

Complete models—not just single operators—built by composing Triton kernels and running across the iGPU and NPU.

| Model | Description | Datatype(s) | Example |
|:------|:------------|:------------|:--------|
| [GPT-2](gpt2/) | End-to-end GPT-2 inference (all four sizes: small/medium/large/xl) composed from Triton kernels, running across iGPU and NPU. | bf16 | [gpt2/](gpt2/) |
| [Qwen2.5](qwen2_5/) | End-to-end Qwen2.5-Instruct inference (0.5B/1.5B) composed from Triton kernels, with KV-cached autoregressive generation running across iGPU and NPU. | bf16 | [qwen2_5/](qwen2_5/) |
| [Llama-3.2-1B (Q4NX)](llama32_1b_q4nx/) | End-to-end Llama-3.2-1B on the NPU: a Triton prefill built from this repo's kernels, and a decode that runs every layer and the LM head in one Triton superkernel dispatch a token (mlir-air's fused Q4NX decode with --decode npu). | bf16 prefill, q4nx decode | [llama32_1b_q4nx/](llama32_1b_q4nx/) |
| [Llama-3.2-3B (Q4NX)](llama32_3b_q4nx/) | The Llama-3.2-3B configuration of the same Triton prefill and superkernel decode, sharing the llm_q4nx harness. | bf16 prefill, q4nx decode | [llama32_3b_q4nx/](llama32_3b_q4nx/) |
| [Llama-3.1-8B (Q4NX)](llama31_8b_q4nx/) | The Llama-3.1-8B configuration of the same split. The same block as the 1B -- SwiGLU, one norm pair, no qk-norm -- but 32 layers of 4096 against the 1B's 16 of 2048, and an untied LM head. | bf16 prefill, q4nx decode | [llama31_8b_q4nx/](llama31_8b_q4nx/) |
| [Qwen3-4B (Q4NX)](qwen3_4b_q4nx/) | Qwen3-4B on the same Triton prefill and superkernel decode, and the first Q4NX model here that is not Llama-shaped: each head is RMS-normalized between the QKV projection and RoPE. | bf16 prefill, q4nx decode | [qwen3_4b_q4nx/](qwen3_4b_q4nx/) |
| [Qwen3-8B (Q4NX)](qwen3_8b_q4nx/) | Qwen3-4B's block at 4096, reusing its forward unchanged. What it adds is size: an untied LM head, and a decode whose weights no longer fit one buffer. | bf16 prefill, q4nx decode | [qwen3_8b_q4nx/](qwen3_8b_q4nx/) |
| [Qwen2.5-7B (Q4NX)](qwen25_7b_q4nx/) | Llama-shaped but for a bias on the q, k and v projections, which nothing else here has. Its weights are not a bundle either: an upstream checkpoint is quantized on load. | bf16 prefill, q4nx decode | [qwen25_7b_q4nx/](qwen25_7b_q4nx/) |
| [Qwen2.5-3B (Q4NX)](qwen25_3b_q4nx/) | Qwen2.5-7B's block at 2048, on the same biased-QKV forward. The only model here whose mlir-air decode (--decode npu) runs with the dual-channel weight feed off. | bf16 prefill, q4nx decode | [qwen25_3b_q4nx/](qwen25_3b_q4nx/) |
| [Phi-4-mini (Q4NX)](phi4_mini_q4nx/) | Llama-shaped but for the rotation: RoPE covers 96 of each head's 128 lanes, on frequencies read from a LongRoPE table in the bundle. The first model here whose delta is in the operator. | bf16 prefill, q4nx decode | [phi4_mini_q4nx/](phi4_mini_q4nx/) |
| [Gemma3-4B (Q4NX)](gemma3_4b_q4nx/) | Gemma3-4B on the same prefill and decode, and the furthest from the Llama block: a four-norm sandwich, two RoPE thetas chosen per layer, a 1024-token sliding window, and a GELU-tanh GLU. | bf16 prefill, q4nx decode | [gemma3_4b_q4nx/](gemma3_4b_q4nx/) |
| [Gemma4-E2B (Q4NX)](gemma4_e2b_q4nx/) | Gemma3's block plus per-layer embeddings, layers that differ in shape from each other, and twenty that carry no KV cache of their own. Its decode is one Triton superkernel dispatch a token, or with --decode npu mlir-air's per-layer-embedding engine rather than the shared one. | bf16 prefill, q4nx decode | [gemma4_e2b_q4nx/](gemma4_e2b_q4nx/) |
| [Gemma4-E4B (Q4NX)](gemma4_e4b_q4nx/) | Gemma4-E2B's architecture at D 2560 and 42 layers, with two KV heads. mlir-air's fused NPU prefill, and the superkernel decode or mlir-air's per-layer-embedding one. | bf16 prefill, q4nx decode | [gemma4_e4b_q4nx/](gemma4_e4b_q4nx/) |
| [Gemma4-E2B flash (image)](gemma4_e2b_flash/) | An image turn on Gemma4-E2B: the vision tower encodes the image's patches into soft tokens that take the place of the image placeholders in the prompt. The tower, the prefill and the decode each run on the NPU or the iGPU. | bf16 vision + prefill, q4nx decode | [gemma4_e2b_flash/](gemma4_e2b_flash/) |
| [Gemma4-E4B flash (image)](gemma4_e4b_flash/) | Gemma4-E2B flash's image turn on the Gemma4-E4B checkpoint, whose soft tokens are projected to D 2560. | bf16 vision + prefill, q4nx decode | [gemma4_e4b_flash/](gemma4_e4b_flash/) |

## Runtime Features

Backend capabilities rather than single operators, demonstrated end to end.

| Feature | Description | Datatype(s) | Example |
|:--------|:------------|:------------|:--------|
| [Zero-Copy iGPU/NPU Buffers](zero_copy/) | Buffers the iGPU and the NPU can both address, so a tensor handed from one to the other never moves -- with a benchmark of the hand-off with and without copies, under both NPU runtimes. | f32 | [zero_copy/](zero_copy/) |

## Running Examples

Make sure XRT is sourced and a virtual environment with `triton-xdna` is active (see top-level [README](../README.md)):

```bash
source /opt/xilinx/xrt/setup.sh

# Run an example on AIE2 (NPU1):
cd matmul_bf16_m64_n64_k64
AIR_TRANSFORM_TILING_SCRIPT=transform_aie2.mlir python matmul_bf16_m64_n64_k64.py

# Run on AIE2P (NPU2):
AIR_TRANSFORM_TILING_SCRIPT=transform_aie2p.mlir python matmul_bf16_m64_n64_k64.py
```

## Running All Tests

```bash
python scripts/run_tests.py --device aie2 --verbose
python scripts/run_tests.py --device aie2p --verbose
```
